Hi Emma — thanks for the clear notes and for sharing Arcadia's redline. Short answers up front and then proposed next steps:

1) Notice window: Redwood's standard process is a 45-calendar-day advance notice for new subprocessors that will handle customer data (we treat "hosting/processing" subprocessors as in-scope). That window is intended to give customers time to raise objections and for us to provide mitigation information.

2) Objection process: customers get a 10-business-day objection window from the date we post the notice. Objections should be submitted in writing to security@redwood.ai (please CC your procurement contact). Our standard remediation options are: provide additional contractual safeguards, enable data migration assistance, or, in limited cases, discontinue provisioning to that customer while maintaining service continuity via an approved alternative.

3) Execution: we can sign via DocuSign. If you want us to accept your redlines, please mark them and return. Our preference for speed is to sign the current Redwood_Standard_DPA_V3 (attached) and then incorporate any mutually agreed redlines in a dated amendment. If you need a redline-first flow, we can accept that; it will add a brief review cycle.

Attached: Redwood_Standard_DPA_V3_redline.pdf (high-level exceptions noted). Also shared our SOC 2 Type II report link below for Arcadia's security team.

- If you want the redline route, we can have counsel (karthik_iyer) produce a response within 2 business days.

Emma — copying in legal as requested. A couple of clarifying points from a contracting standpoint:

- Notice & objection windows: Redwood's operational position is 45 calendar days notice for new subprocessors that will process customer data. Customers have 10 business days to submit a written objection. We are open to a narrow carve for "data residency" subprocessors where customers can request a 60-calendar-day notice, subject to mutual agreement and documented in a statement of work or amendment.

- "Managed service partners": if a partner is contractually engaged by Redwood and will have access to customer data (including encrypted keys or backups), we classify them as subprocessors and they are in-scope for notice.

- Retroactive amendments: we will not apply amendments retroactively to cover past processing; amendments take effect on the effective date in the amendment and apply prospectively. However, operational mitigations (e.g., pausing onboarding for a given customer, additional logging, escrow of keys) can be configured during the objection period on a case-by-case basis.

If Arcadia prefers 60 days for all categories, that is a commercial ask that we can present to sales leadership — it may impact pricing/commitments. If you’re amenable to a targeted 60-day carve for only "data residency" or "hosting" subprocessors, we can accept that as a compromise.

I reviewed Arcadia's redline briefly and added a few comments; I'll follow up with a marked PDF this afternoon. If you want to expedite, Rachel can send the DocuSign envelope for the current DPA and we can continue redlines as an amendment.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
